_comment: The hard cases, with NO recipe hint. The model is on its own against the things that actually break element-picking on real websites. If these pass with no hint, the AI is genuinely reading the page rather than leaning on the recipe.

cases.note: No hint at all. 'Tourism Packages' in the menu contains a-g-e, and comes first in the document.

cases.goal: show me more about the first train
cases.note: The icon-only button. Its glyph is aria-hidden, so the only name it has is its aria-label.
Placeholder but no label. Must not be confused with 'Email address (optional)' beside it.

TWO right answers, and which one is rung decides whether a stop was due. The payment page holds an empty Card number box AND a Pay button, and "pay for the ticket" can reasonably mean either: the card has to be typed before Pay can be pressed. A text box cannot take money, so ringing it needs no stop. Ringing Pay DOES, and dangerousNames keeps that check alive independently of the gate rules, so a regression in safety.js would still be caught here.

cases.goal: I want to cancel a ticket I booked
cases.note: Three valid answers: the page has all three as LINKS, and a reasonable guide could point at any of them. None gates, because a cancel link navigates to a cancellation page where the real button lives and gets stopped on arrival. Stopping someone on the way there is a false stop, and a stop that fires on the way to a page is one people learn to dismiss.

cases.goal: I want to read the cancellation rules
cases.note: GATE MUST NOT FIRE, for two independent reasons: it is a link rather than a control, and 'cancellation' with no booking word would not trip the word list anyway.

cases.goal: choose whether the passenger is male or female
cases.note: Must pick the Gender dropdown, not the Berth preference one next to it.
